Rashi on Berakhot 25b:10:2.hebrew: ברוק - רוקק עליה ומכסה אותה ברוק:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:10:2.english: With spittle - He spits on it and covers it with spittle.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:12:2.hebrew: וכמה מיא רמי ואזיל - כמה ישליך לתוכם ויבטלם? הלא מרובין הם:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:12:2.english: And how much water can he keep pouring - How much [water] can he pour into them and nullify them? Are they not plentiful?

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:12:3.hebrew: ומי רגלים - מועטין, והם בכלי, והוא בא לקרות ק"ש אצלם:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:12:3.english: And urine - [Where it is] a small amount, and it is in a vessel, and he comes to recite the Shema near it.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:14:1.hebrew: לבסוף - שמי רגלים בכלי, וזה נותן לתוכן מים — בההיא קאמר ר' זכאי: רביעית:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:14:1.english: Afterward - Where urine is in the vessel and one puts water into it — in that [case], Rabbi Zakkai said: A quarter [of a log].

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:14:2.hebrew: אבל לכתחלה - שקדמו המים למי רגלים, דברי הכל: כל שהוא. שכשמטיל מי רגלים בכלי לבסוף, ראשון ראשון שנופל לתוך המים מתבטל, ואע"פ שהם רבים והולכין — כבר בטלו:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:14:2.english: However, at the beginning - Where the water preceded the urine, all agree [that] any amount [is sufficient]. For when one discharges urine into the vessel afterward, each first [drop] that falls into the water is nullified; and even though they are many and continue [to flow], they have already been nullified.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:15:1.english: Bring me a quarter [of a log] - Even initially.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:16:1.hebrew: גרף ועביט - שניהם כלי חרס הם, אלא של רעי קרוי גרף, ושל מי רגלים קרוי עביט:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:16:1.english: A graf and an avit - Both of them are earthenware vessels, but [the one] for excrement is called a graf, and [the one] for urine is called an avit.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:16:2.hebrew: אסור לקרות ק"ש כנגדם - הואיל ומיוחדין לכך, ואע"פ שאין בתוכן כלום:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:16:2.english: It is forbidden to recite the Shema opposite them - Since they are designated for this [purpose], even though there is nothing inside them.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:16:3.english: And urine itself - In a vessel that is not designated for it.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:16:4.english: Whether in front of the bed - Where the bed does not intervene between him and them.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:16:5.hebrew: בין לאחר המטה - שהמטה מפסקת ביניהם, אסור:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:16:5.english: Whether behind the bed - Where the bed separates between them, it is forbidden.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:16:6.english: "Or he places them beneath the bed" is our reading - And we do not read: "A vessel within a vessel."

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:16:7.english: Under the bed - As if they were buried in the ground.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:19:1.english: Our dilemma has been resolved for us - Our question has been clarified regarding the distinction between in front of the bed and behind the bed.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:19:2.english: The baraitot, however, contradict [each other] - For their positions were switched.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:1:1.hebrew: בטופח ע"מ להטפיח איכא בינייהו - ת"ק בעי על מנת להטפיח, ור' יוסי מחמיר:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:1:1.english: [The difference] between them is regarding [whether it is] moist enough to moisten [other things] - The first tanna requires [that it be moist enough] to moisten [other things], and Rabbi Yosei is [more] stringent.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:21:1.english: Who did you hear, etc. - I do not know where it is.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:22:1.hebrew: פשיטא לי - במניחן תחת המטה, ורגליה קצרים שאין הימנה ולקרקע שלשה טפחים — כלבוד דמי, והרי הן כטמונים:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:22:1.english: It is obvious to me - In [a case where] one places them under the bed, and its legs are short, such that there are not three handbreadths between it and the ground — it is considered connected [lavud], and behold, they are as if concealed.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:22:2.hebrew: עשרה ודאי - לא שאלתי ממנו, דנראה כאילו אינה תחתיה; מאחר שיש הפסק כל כך, אין זה כסוי:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:22:2.english: Ten [handbreadths], certainly - I did not ask him [about this], for it appears as though it is not underneath it; since there is such an interval, this is not a covering.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:24:1.hebrew: עייליה לחופה ולא הוה מסתייעא מילתא - דנישואין, שלא היה יכול לבעול:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:24:1.english: He brought him into the wedding canopy, and the matter did not succeed - [The matter] of marriage — that he was not able to consummate [the marriage].

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:24:2.hebrew: סכנתון לברי - כמעט סכנתם את בני למות בעונש העון:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:24:2.english: You [would have] endangered my son - You almost endangered my son [causing him] to die through the punishment for the sin.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:2:1.hebrew: לימא תנא סתמא כר' אליעזר - והלכה כמותו:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:2:1.english: Shall we say that the tanna taught anonymously in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer - And [consequently] the halakha is in accordance with him?

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:3:1.hebrew: דילמא לותיקין - קאמרה מתני' עם הנץ החמה, אבל לכ"ע עד שלש שעות:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:3:1.english: Perhaps for the vatikin - The mishna said [to recite] with sunrise, but for everyone [else, the time extends] until three hours.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:4:1.hebrew: והרי לבו רואה את הערוה - קס"ד: כל אבר שאין דרכו לראות את הערוה, [ורואה] אותו בשעה שקורא בתורה — קרינן ביה: "ולא יראה בך ערות דבר":
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:4:1.english: And behold, his heart sees the nakedness - [The Gemara] initially assumed: Any limb [or organ] that does not normally see the nakedness, and [it] sees it while he is reading the Torah — we apply to it: “And He shall not see in you any naked thing.”

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:8:1.hebrew: לא נתנה תורה למלאכי השרת - שאין להם ערוה, על כרחנו יש לנו ערוה, ואין אנו יכולים להשמר מכל זה:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:8:1.english: The Torah was not given to the ministering angels - For they have no nakedness; [whereas] we, of necessity, have nakedness, and we cannot guard against all this.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:9:1.hebrew: בעששית - לנטירנ"א בלע"ז — כלומר, מחיצת זכוכית או קלף דק מפסיק בנתיים, והיא נראית:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:9:1.english: In a lantern - Lanterne in Old French; that is to say, a partition of glass or thin parchment separates in between, and it is visible.

Rashi on Berakhot 25b:9:2.hebrew: בכסוי תליא מילתא - וכסית את צאתך:
Rashi on Berakhot 25b:9:2.english: The matter depends on covering - [As it is written:] "And you shall cover your excrement" (Deuteronomy 23:14).

Tosafot on Berakhot 25b:16:2.hebrew: ובלבד שיטיל בהן רביעית מים - אבל בגרף, אפשר דלא מהני מים:
Tosafot on Berakhot 25b:16:2.english: "Provided that he pours a revi'it of water into them" - But regarding a graf [chamber pot for excrement], it is possible that water does not help.

Tosafot on Berakhot 25b:4:1.hebrew: והרי לבו רואה את הערוה - פירש ר"י: מדפריך גמרא הכי בפשיטות, משמע דלבו רואה את הערוה אסור. אלא דרבינו שמעיה, תלמידו של רש"י, פסק כת"ק, דלבו רואה את הערוה מותר. ומיהו בסמוך משמע דאסור, דלא פליגי הני אמוראי אלא בעקבו רואה את הערוה, אבל בלבו רואה את הערוה כ"ע מודו דאסור:
Tosafot on Berakhot 25b:4:1.english: "And doesn't his heart see [his] nakedness?" - The Ri explained: Since the Gemara asks this so simply, it implies that [when] one's heart sees [his] nakedness, it is forbidden. However, Rabbeinu Shemayah, the student of Rashi, ruled in accordance with the first tanna, that [when] one's heart sees [his] nakedness, it is permitted. Nevertheless, nearby it implies that it is forbidden, for these Amoraim disagree only regarding [a case where] one's heel sees [his] nakedness, but regarding [a case where] one's heart sees [his] nakedness, everyone agrees that it is forbidden.

Tosafot on Berakhot 25b:8:1.hebrew: והלכתא נוגע עקבו אסור - וטעמא דגזרינן נוגע עקבו — שמא יגע בידיו:
Tosafot on Berakhot 25b:8:1.english: "And the halakha is: [If] his heel touches, it is forbidden" - And the reason that we decree [against] his heel touching [the nakedness is] lest he touch [it] with his hands.
